easy.def: A woman of high rank in a royal family.
examples: The duchess lived in a castle.
A duchess wears a crown.
We read about a duchess.

more.def: A woman of very high rank in some countries, or the wife of a duke.
examples: The duchess waved to the crowd from her carriage.
In the fairy tale, the duchess lives in a grand castle.
The painting showed a duchess in a long silk gown.

easy.def: A bird that swims and quacks.
examples: The duck swims.
Ducks quack.
A duck has webbed feet.

more.def: A water bird with a flat beak, webbed feet and a quack.
examples: The duck paddled across the pond.
Baby ducks follow their mother.
A duck dipped its head under the water.

easy.def: To bend down quickly.
examples: Duck under the branch.
He ducked his head.
She ducked under the rope.

more.def: To bend or move down quickly to get out of the way.
examples: She ducked under the low branch.
He ducked when the ball flew by.
We ducked under the table.

easy.def: A little duck, or a duck toy.
examples: My rubber ducky floats.
A yellow ducky.
The ducky is in the tub.

more.def: A word for a duck, especially a small, yellow rubber duck used as a bath toy.
examples: My rubber ducky floats in the tub.
The baby giggled at the yellow ducky.
A line of little duckies floated across the water.

easy.def: A pipe or tube that carries air or liquid.
examples: The air comes out of the duct.
A duct is in the ceiling.
A tear duct is by your eye.

more.def: A tube or pipe that carries air, liquid or wires from one place to another.
examples: Warm air flows through a duct in the ceiling.
Tears flow out through a small duct near the eye.
The workers cleaned the dust out of the air duct.

easy.def: Something that does not work.
examples: The firework was a dud.
This battery is a dud.
The toy was a dud.

more.def: Something that does not work the way it should, or that turns out to be a disappointment.
examples: The firework was a dud and fizzled out without a bang.
We bought a battery, but it was a dud and the toy would not move.
The movie was a dud, and many people left early.

easy.def: A friendly word for a boy or man.
examples: Hey, dude!
That dude is tall.
My cousin is a cool dude.

more.def: A casual word for a man or boy, often used to talk to a friend.
examples: Hey dude, wait for me!
That dude on the skateboard is really good.
Some people call their friends dude.

easy.def: Expected or needed by a time.
examples: The paper is due Friday.
The bus is due at three.
My book is due.

more.def: Expected or needing to be done by a certain time.
examples: My library book is due on Friday.
The train is due at four o'clock.
The report is due next week.

easy.def: A fight between two people from long ago.
examples: They read about a duel in the story.
The duel was long ago.
A duel is in the old tale.

more.def: A formal fight between two people that took place in the past to settle an argument, or any contest between two sides.
examples: In the old story, two knights agreed to a duel to settle the argument.
The chess match turned into a duel between the two best players.
The two quick chess players had a long duel before the winner was clear.

easy.def: A man with a very high rank in some countries.
examples: The duke lived in a castle.
The king spoke to the duke.
A duke is a kind of lord.

more.def: A man of very high rank, just below a prince or a king.
examples: The duke lived in a huge castle on a hill.
In the story, the duke gave a grand party for the whole town.
A duke often owned a lot of land long ago.

easy.def: Not sharp.
examples: The knife is dull.
The scissors are dull.
My pencil is dull.

more.def: Not sharp, or not shiny or interesting.
examples: The knife was too dull to cut the bread.
The old penny was dull and brown.
The long talk was dull.

easy.def: Silly or not smart.
examples: That was a dumb mistake.
It was a dumb joke.
I felt dumb when I forgot my name.

more.def: Showing poor thinking; silly. It can hurt when used to name-call someone.
examples: Leaving the gate open was a dumb mistake.
He made a dumb joke that no one laughed at.
She felt dumb when she forgot her lines.

easy.def: A model of a person.
examples: The store has a dummy in the window.
The dummy wears a hat.
The dummy is made of plastic.

more.def: A model of a person's body, used to show clothes or to practice on.
examples: The shop window had a dummy wearing a winter coat.
Doctors practiced on a dummy.
A dummy stood in the corner of the tailor's shop.

easy.def: To drop or pour out a lot of something.
examples: Dump the sand out.
He dumped the toys on the floor.
The truck dumped the dirt.

more.def: To drop or pour out a heap of something.
examples: The truck dumped a pile of gravel on the road.
She dumped the puzzle pieces onto the table.
Do not dump trash in the river.

easy.def: A place where trash is taken.
examples: We took the trash to the dump.
The dump is outside town.
The truck drove to the dump.

more.def: A place where garbage is taken and left.
examples: The garbage truck drove to the dump.
Seagulls fly over the town dump.
We took the old couch to the dump.

easy.def: A soft ball or pocket of dough that is cooked.
examples: I ate a dumpling.
The soup has dumplings.
We made dumplings.

more.def: A small ball or pocket of dough that is boiled, steamed or fried, often with a filling or in soup.
examples: We ate steamed dumplings filled with vegetables for dinner.
Grandma put fluffy dumplings in the chicken soup.
She folded the dough around the filling to make a dumpling.

easy.def: A big metal bin for trash.
examples: The trash goes in the dumpster.
The dumpster is full.
A dumpster is behind the store.

more.def: A very large metal container used to hold trash and be hauled away.
examples: Workers threw the old boards into the dumpster.
A big green dumpster stood behind the school.
The truck came to empty the dumpster on Monday.

easy.def: A hill of sand made by the wind.
examples: We climbed the dune.
The sand dune is high.
The dune shifted.

more.def: A hill of loose sand that is piled up by the wind, found in deserts and along beaches.
examples: We climbed to the top of the tall sand dune and slid down.
The wind shaped the dunes into smooth waves.
Camels crossed the dunes of the desert.

easy.def: A dark prison room under a castle.
examples: The dungeon is dark.
The knight was in the dungeon.
A dungeon is in the castle.

more.def: A dark underground room in a castle, used long ago as a prison.
examples: The dungeon was dark and cold.
In the story, the knight was locked in the dungeon.
A dungeon is below the castle.

easy.def: To dip something into a liquid for a moment.
examples: I dunk a chip in dip.
She dunked the bread.
He dunked his hand in the water.

more.def: To dip something quickly into a liquid.
examples: I dunk my cookie in milk.
She dunked her bread into the soup.
He dunked the apple in water to wash it.

easy.def: To jump and push a basketball down through the hoop.
examples: He can dunk the ball.
She dunked it.
The player dunked.

more.def: To jump up and push a basketball down through the hoop with force.
examples: The tall player can dunk the ball.
He jumped up and dunked the ball with one hand.
The crowd cheered when she dunked the ball.

easy.def: An exact copy of something.
examples: I have a duplicate of my key.
This is a duplicate.
She made a duplicate.

more.def: An exact copy of something.
examples: I have a duplicate of the key in case I lose it.
This card is a duplicate of one I already have.
She made a duplicate of the picture for her friend.

easy.def: To make an exact copy of something.
examples: I duplicate the key.
The machine duplicates papers.
She duplicated the picture.

more.def: To make an exact copy of something.
examples: The machine can duplicate a key in a minute.
She duplicated the picture so both friends had one.
It is hard to duplicate the taste of Grandma's soup.

easy.def: At some time while something goes on.
examples: We talk during lunch.
It rained during the night.
Do not talk during the movie.

more.def: Throughout the time that something goes on, or at some point in it.
examples: The bears sleep during the winter.
It rained several times during the night.
Please stay quiet during the show.

easy.def: Tiny bits of dry dirt in the air or on things.
examples: Dust is on the shelf.
The wind blew dust.
I sneezed from the dust.

more.def: Very small bits of dry dirt or other stuff that collect on things or float in the air.
examples: A thick layer of dust covered the old books.
The truck kicked up a cloud of dust on the dirt road.
A sunbeam showed the dust floating in the air.

easy.def: To wipe the tiny bits of dirt off things.
examples: I dust the table.
She dusted the shelf.
Please dust your room.

more.def: To clean a shelf or table by wiping off the fine powder that settles on it.
examples: He dusted the bookshelves every Saturday.
Mom asked me to dust the furniture.
I dusted the piano with a soft cloth.

easy.def: Covered with dust.
examples: The shelf is dusty.
A dusty road.
The old book is dusty.

more.def: Covered with a layer of fine dust.
examples: The shelf was dusty.
We drove down a dusty road.
The old book was dusty.

easy.def: A job you must do.
examples: It is my duty to feed the fish.
Her duty is to hand out papers.
Setting the table is my duty.

more.def: Something that you must do because it is your job or the right thing to do.
examples: It is a lifeguard's duty to watch the swimmers.
Feeding the dog is my duty each morning.
Voting is a duty of every adult citizen.
